documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Texted at lunch about burning again, came in after dismissal.

S: 3 days dysuria, urgency, urine cloudy and "smells off." No fever or chills. No flank pain. No visible blood. Last episode in November grew Proteus, cleared on cephalexin.

O: afebrile, vitals fine. Abdomen soft, mild suprapubic discomfort, no CVA tenderness.
UA: cloudy, pH 8.0, LE+, nitrite+, 60 WBC, blood negative.

A/P: recurrent cystitis, likely same organism. It was sensitive to TMP-SMX last time, so TMP-SMX DS BID x3 days. Culture sent. If she has another one this spring we should think about why they keep coming back.

documents.body: Proteus mirabilis again, sensitive to TMP-SMX. Current treatment appropriate. MA to let her know.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Follow-up, urinary symptoms again.

She says the infections never really go away. After each course she feels better for a few weeks, then the urine is cloudy and foul-smelling again. Over the last few months she has also noticed an ache in the right flank that comes and goes, sometimes for an afternoon, then nothing for a week or two. No fever, no chills, no blood in the urine. No vomiting. Bowels normal.

Exam: afebrile, BP normal. Appears well. Abdomen soft, nontender. Mild tenderness at the right CVA; left nontender.
UA: cloudy, pH 8.0, LE+, nitrite+, 20 WBC, no blood.

Assessment: recurrent UTI, Proteus on both cultures since November, persistently alkaline urine, now with intermittent right flank pain. Not acutely ill.

Plan:
- Cephalexin 500 BID x7d, culture sent.
- BMP today for kidney function.
- Urology referral to look for a structural cause. Order placed, she prefers late July, after the school year.
- To the ED for fever, vomiting or severe pain.

documents.title: Culture and BMP
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Culture Proteus again, sensitive to cephalexin. Kidney function normal. Urology referral already sent.

conditions.label: Kidney stone
conditions.note: 7 mm right lower pole calculus on KUB

reports.text: Single supine view of the abdomen. A 7 mm radiopaque calculus projects over the lower pole of the right kidney. No other calcification along the expected course of either ureter or in the pelvis. Left renal shadow without calculus. Nonobstructive bowel gas pattern. Osseous structures unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: 7 mm right lower pole renal calculus.

documents.title: Urology Consultation
documents.author: urology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE UROLOGY GROUP - NEW PATIENT CONSULTATION
Date of service: 07/21/2025
Re: Kelly Bergeron, DOB 10/13/1990
Referred by: primary care

Reason for referral: recurrent urinary tract infections.

History: 34-year-old teacher with repeated infections over the past year. Her PCP has treated them with several antibiotic courses; she describes each one as improving her symptoms without ever fully clearing them. For a few months she has had an intermittent right flank ache and urine that is cloudy and foul-smelling. She has had no fevers or chills and has not seen blood. Cultures from her primary care office have grown Proteus mirabilis three times, with alkaline urine each time.

Medications: none currently.
Allergies: NKDA.
Past surgical history: none.
Family history: mother with nephrolithiasis; father with hypertension.
Social history: never smoker; alcohol occasionally, one or two drinks a month; elementary school teacher.

Exam: vital signs normal. Comfortable. Abdomen soft without masses. Mild right costovertebral angle tenderness. No suprapubic tenderness.

Imaging: KUB obtained in clinic today, personally reviewed: 7 mm radiopaque calculus over the right lower pole. No ureteral or bladder calculi.

Impression:
1. Right renal calculus, 7 mm.
2. Recurrent UTI with a urease-producing organism and alkaline urine. The stone may well be infection related and could be acting as a reservoir.

Plan:
- Fluids, at least 2.5 liters daily.
- Urine culture with any symptoms; treat per sensitivities.
- We discussed elective ureteroscopy to remove the stone versus watching it. She would like time to think and would rather not schedule anything during the school year.
- Return in 6 months with repeat imaging, sooner for fever or severe pain.

Urology

documents.title: Kidney stone question
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, I saw urology last week and they found a kidney stone on the right. They gave me the option of having it taken out or waiting. Did you get their letter? Mom had stones too so I'm not totally shocked. Is waiting ok?

documents.title: RE: Kidney stone question
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Kelly, yes, the letter came in and I read it. Waiting is a reasonable option for now, and the urologist will re-image you in about 6 months. Keep up the water. If you get fever, vomiting, or pain that won't settle, go to the ER. Happy to talk it through by phone if helpful.

documents.body: Here for seasonal vaccines. Feeling well, no fever. No prior vaccine reactions. Flu 0.5 mL IM left arm, 2025-26 COVID (Moderna) IM right arm. VIS reviewed. Observed 15 min, no reaction. Asked about her urine: no infections since June.
